clue.text: Flog ancient doorstep

parts.note: to thresh is to beat or flail, as grain is beaten
ancient means old

explanation.surface: An order to beat an antique doorstep, or to sell off an old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' reads as British slang for sell, but here it means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep is the sill at an entrance, the strip you cross going in.

clue.text: Propose returning pieces of Melba toast

indicators.note: returning means the run of letters is read backwards
pieces of means the letters are taken from inside the phrase Melba toast

explanation.surface: Suggesting that bits of crisp thin toast be sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of' takes ELBAT from inside 'Melba toast'; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage, to table a motion is to put it forward formally for discussion.

clue.text: Managed firm united by Republican spite

parts.note: managed, as in ran a business
CO is short for company, a firm
U is the usual abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A company boss teams up with a Republican out of malice.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name bitter, lasting ill will toward someone.

clue.text: Botanist losing head travelling to Waterloo perhaps

indicators.note: travelling suggests the remaining letters moving about into a new order
losing head drops the first letter of the word Botanist

explanation.surface: A plant scientist, now beheaded, journeys to Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' leaves OTANIST, which 'travelling' rearranges. Waterloo is a major London rail terminus, not the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is an example of a railway terminus, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Church coated in mineral paint type

indicators.note: coated in places the church abbreviation inside the mineral word

parts.note: ore is a mineral from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A church covered in a type of mineral-based paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment used as a colour in paint.

clue.text: Cleaner put off by posh bloke

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a gent is a gentleman, a refined man

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is discouraged by an upper-class man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' suggests a person; it is the washing product.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleaning agent used for washing.

clue.text: Terrible actor was famously useless Lear first of all

indicators.note: first of all takes the opening letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: A review: this actor's King Lear was notoriously bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for something very bad.

clue.text: Assigned practical was relevant

definitions.meaning: ... paint or funds, meaning put to a use or assigned
... science is practical rather than theoretical
a rule that ... was relevant to the case

explanation.surface: A practical task was set, and it mattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: put to use, put into practice rather than theory, and bore on the matter.

clue.text: Little cakes cooked in cafes

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are fiddled, like cooked books

explanation.surface: Small cakes baked in coffee shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancies are small iced cakes, as in French fancies, a British teatime treat.

clue.text: Settled debtors notes involving US soldier that's quick to sue

parts.note: lit, as a bird lit on a branch, means settled

indicators.note: involving means the debtors' notes wrap around the soldier

parts.note: IOUs are written notes of debt
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone who settles debts, juggling IOUs and an American soldier, is always ready to sue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' suggests paying a debt, but here it means alighted.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigious person is fond of going to law, quick to take others to court.

clue.text: Live with great husband in a lower position

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
neat is slang for great or excellent

explanation.surface: Advice to live happily with a wonderful husband, though lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: Both say something is below or underneath something else.

clue.text: Hairpiece to secure across priest's head

indicators.note: across means the pair to and secure sit on either side of the next letter

parts.note: to knot something is to secure it

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word priest's

explanation.surface: A wig to be fastened over a cleric's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft or bun of hair worn on the crown, or an ornament there.

clue.text: European cause is controversial

parts.note: a motive is a reason or cause for acting

explanation.surface: A European cause stirs up debate.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive issue arouses strong feeling, which makes it contentious.

clue.text: Mocking metal barrier

definitions.meaning: a fence of upright metal bars

explanation.surface: Jeering at a steel fence.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the verb form of rail, to rant scornfully, and a row of bars forming a fence.

clue.text: The Parisian follows deplorable account

indicators.note: follows puts the French article after the word for deplorable

parts.note: chronic is British informal for very bad or deplorable
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: The Frenchman comes after a shocking report.
explanation.walkthrough: CHRONIC in this sense is British slang for dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical record, an account of events in order.

clue.text: Throw a bag and small instruments

parts.note: to cast is to throw
to net is to catch or bag

explanation.surface: Toss a sack and some little instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Castanets are hand-held percussion instruments clicked together in Spanish dance.

clue.text: Agreement about bit of society covered by official count

indicators.note: covered by puts the about word and a letter inside the official count

parts.note: a census is an official count of the population
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: bit of takes the first letter of the word society

explanation.surface: Accord about part of society found in the national census.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is general agreement among a group.

clue.text: Dance in circle repeatedly

parts.note: a disc is a flat circle
repeatedly calls for another circle, the ring-shaped letter O

explanation.surface: Dancing round in a circle again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circle repeatedly' gives two circles: a DISC, then O.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club where people dance to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Water vapour from running water (not river)

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the river letter

parts.note: a stream is flowing water

explanation.surface: Vapour rising from flowing water, though not a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is water turned to gas by boiling.

clue.text: Attention given to story run previously

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention
a story is a lie, a fib
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A newspaper story given attention that ran before.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at a time before now.

clue.text: One helping with delivery of male fish to mate

parts.note: id, or ide, is a freshwater fish
to wife is an old verb for marrying, taking as a mate

explanation.surface: Someone delivering a male fish so it can breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests the post; it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: A midwife is trained to help women through childbirth.

clue.text: Suitor on inappropriately embracing love becomes infamous

indicators.note: embracing means the shuffled letters wrap around the love letter
inappropriately suggests the letters set out in an improper order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A suitor who behaves badly in his embraces earns a bad name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone well known for something bad.

clue.text: Hit drink to form connection

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Knocking back a drink to bond with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious relationship or bond.

clue.text: Address old fixed allowance

parts.note: a ration is a fixed portion

explanation.surface: A speech about an old set allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' could be a street location; here it is a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, an address.

clue.text: Cut short a card game

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four

explanation.surface: A game of cards ended early.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it.

clue.text: Asks secretary to return rings

indicators.note: to return means the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
peals are rings of bells

explanation.surface: Someone requests that their secretary return the calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' looks like phone calls but means bell-ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal is to ask earnestly for something.

clue.text: Serious wound admitted to A & E

indicators.note: admitted to puts the injury inside, like a patient admitted to hospital

parts.note: a cut is a wound

explanation.surface: A serious injury taken into the casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: A & E is a British hospital's Accident and Emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute illness is severe and urgent, so serious.

clue.text: Arson destroyed location device

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A fire-setter wrecks a tracking gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar locates objects underwater by sound echoes.

clue.text: Sire mixed about 59 potions

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the number
mixed means the letters of Sire are jumbled

parts.note: LIX is 59 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A father mixes some fifty-nine magic drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' scrambles SIRE to ELIRS; 'about' wraps it round the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Elixirs are magical or medicinal potions.

clue.text: Perfect university head I paint regularly

parts.note: the top is the head of something

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word paint

explanation.surface: A university principal paints routinely and flawlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian means idealised, like an imagined perfect society.

clue.text: Wait to look over recreational vehicle

indicators.note: over means the look word lies over and around the vehicle

parts.note: to see is to look

explanation.surface: Someone asked to linger while a camper van is inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait on people is to serve them food and drink.

clue.text: Teens were treated as bribe

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters processed into a different form

explanation.surface: Teenagers were given a treat as an inducement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is slang for an inducement or bribe.
